note: Bullets per operator and reform from the Nov 13 and Nov 16, 2026 filings, each citing a reading and page with a verbatim quote. `by` names a filer other than the operator (its transmission owners, or one owner as an example). null means SPP has not filed; its response is due Nov 20, 2026.

study.t: One Fast Energization Process studies load and generator requests together
study.quote: which will study together New Service Requests, including Generation Interconnection Requests, and requests from Eligible Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of Eligible Load

study.t: Studies complete in 12 months, half the time of today's cycle
study.quote: The Fast Energization Process proposes key reforms to the existing process to complete studies in 12 months

study.t: Screening phase of about four months: two rounds of under 60 days each
study.quote: This accelerated Screening Phase will extend for approximately four months, thereby providing two quick rounds of analysis that each take less than 60 days

study.t: Readiness Deposits posted with the application, at risk at Decision Points I and II
study.quote: having Readiness Deposits posted with the Applications and at risk at Decision Points I and II

cost.t: Large loads make a minimum contribution to TO revenue requirements, with shortfall payments and financial security
cost.quote: to make a minimum contribution towards transmission owners’ revenue requirements, along with a shortfall payment and crediting mechanism and financial security obligations

cost.t: Fast Energization upgrade costs go to the large-load zones for 15 years
cost.quote: this allocation methodology will apply to each portfolio of IRRs identified through PJM’s Fast Energization Process for 15 years

cost.t: A Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement is a condition of entering the process
cost.quote: The Fast Energization Process requires Eligible Customers seeking service on behalf of Large Loads to enter into a Transmission Owner Cost Recovery Agreement as a condition of entering the process

cost.t: Upgrade drivers and capital costs posted on pjm.com in one searchable place
cost.quote: PJM will post the required system topology, the drivers of the need for the IRRs, and their capital costs on pjm.com in a single, accessible, and searchable location

colo.t: Netting of behind-the-meter generation capped at 50 MW
colo.quote: PJM is proposing revisions to Part III, section 34.2 and Schedule 8 of the RAA to implement the 50 MW netting limit

colo.t: Rates for the three new services largely those FERC approved in the co-location paper hearing
colo.quote: The rates for these services are largely identical to those proposed by the PJM Transmission Owners and approved by the Commission in the Co-Located Load Paper Hearing Order

flex.t: Adopts the three new transmission services FERC put forward
flex.quote: PJM also proposes implementing the three new transmission services the Commission put forward in a way that will ensure reliability

flex.t: Interim NITS: interruptible use of spare headroom while upgrades are built
flex.quote: Interim NITS is a transmission service that allows Eligible Customers serving Eligible Load or Large Load to utilize head room on the system as-available on an interruptible basis

flex.t: Interim NITS is energy-only, not capacity-backed
flex.quote: Interim NITS is an energy-only service (i.e., it is not capacity backed).

flex.t: Firm Contract Demand service curtailed on par with NITS and firm point-to-point
flex.quote: FCD Transmission Service will be treated as equivalent to NITS and Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Services for purposes of Curtailment.

proximate.t: Generation and load studied together in one cycle; upgrades optimized for the whole cohort
proximate.quote: Generation and load studied together in one Cycle; IRRs optimized for the whole cohort; interim deliverability schedules

proximate.t: Joint study meant to yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation
proximate.quote: to optimize the Transmission System and yield efficiencies for electrically proximate load and generation

study.t: Large Load Project Review (LLPR) for new loads of 50 MW+ or existing loads growing 25 MW+
study.quote: establishes the LLPR process for new loads of 50 MW or more and existing loads increasing by at least 25 MW in the aggregate

study.t: Three study cycles a year; deadlines posted at least 90 days ahead
study.quote: Requires LLPR studies three times in a 365-day period with application deadlines posted at least 90 calendar days in advance.

study.t: Deposits and project milestones to discourage speculative requests
study.quote: The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.

study.t: TO study report must name the alternative transmission technologies and GETs considered
study.quote: requires Large Load Transmission Customers to include with their LLLPR Application the applicable Transmission Owner’s Interconnection Study Report, specifically identifying what ATTs and GETs were considered

cost.t: Large loads bear the cost of Large Load Upgrades through cost recovery agreements
cost.quote: designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are born by such customers

cost.t: LLPR results published: location and estimated cost of each large load
cost.quote: The results of the LLPR periodically will be published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with Large Load facilities in the MISO region

colo.t: Co-located load needs the generator's interconnection agreement (e.g. a ZGIA) executed first
colo.quote: if the applicants are looking to co-locate the Load with the generation, then they will need to ensure that an appropriate Interconnection Agreement e.g. “ZGIA” has already been executed for the generator

colo.t: GRITS contract demand service is not limited to co-located loads
colo.quote: is not limited to Large Load being served by a co-located generator

flex.t: GRITS: permanent firm and non-firm contract demand service for loads that limit withdrawals
flex.quote: GRITS provides a permanent firm and non-firm contract demand-based, Transmission Service option for Large Loads willing and able to limit their withdrawals under specified price and reliability conditions.

flex.t: Example: a 500 MW load takes 200 MW firm, the rest non-firm
flex.quote: a Large Load Transmission Customer representing a Large Load of 500 MW may desire to only take 200 MW of firm transmission service

flex.t: Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS for staged build-out
flex.quote: The new Transmission Services available to Large Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.

proximate.t: Loads of 200 MW+ partnered with a generator for 15+ years use the LARS study
proximate.quote: If the Large Load is greater than or equal to 200 MW and has formally partnered with a generator for a minimum of fifteen years, then the applicants will go through the LARS study process.

proximate.t: Paired generation capped at 150% of the load's peak, in the same Local Resource Zone
proximate.quote: limits the requested interconnection service to 150 percent of the paired load’s peak demand, and requires the load and generation to be located in the same Local Resource Zone

study.t: Transmission owners (PTOs) keep studying load requests under their own tariffs
study.quote: the PTOs will continue to govern and study all load interconnection requests pursuant to their tariffs

study.t: CAISO reviews each PTO study against its planning models
study.quote: the CAISO will review PTO load interconnection studies to confirm that study assumptions, load characteristics, and results are consistent with the CAISO’s planning models

study.t: $500,000 cash study deposit plus $1,000 per MW of security
study.quote: The study deposit requirement includes a $500,000 cash deposit and financial security in the amount of $1,000 per MW of requested maximum load

study.t: $250,000 study deposit; readiness deposit of twice that
study.quote: an Interconnection Study Deposit of $250,000, a Commercial Readiness Deposit equal to two times the study deposit

cost.t: Cost allocation set in PTO tariffs, not CAISO's
cost.quote: the CAISO believes it is prudent for cost allocation rules to be set forth in the PTO tariffs rather than the CAISO tariff

cost.t: Network-upgrade cost data posted on CAISO's website, searchable
cost.quote: The CAISO agrees that cost data should be transparent and can be provided on the CAISO website in a searchable format.

cost.t: 15-year minimum revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security
cost.quote: a 15-year minimum transmission revenue obligation backed by 5 years of security

cost.t: Security of 5× the minimum annual revenue obligation
cost.quote: a Financial Security requirement equal to five (5) times the Minimum Annual Revenue Obligation

colo.t: Generator interconnection customers must disclose plans to serve co-located load
colo.quote: requires generator interconnection customers to disclose plans to serve co- located load

colo.t: Backup-only or non-exporting behind-the-meter generation handled under retail rules, not CAISO's
colo.quote: These will include large loads with back-up generation only to be used during outages or islanding, and large loads with non-exporting behind-the-meter generation.

flex.t: Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI): energize before network upgrades finish
flex.quote: The CAISO’s Flexible Interim Load Interconnection (FILI) can permit earlier energization while network upgrades are pending

flex.t: Permanent flexible service left for later work
flex.quote: with additional work planned on permanent flexibility and other emerging configurations

flex.t: Interim service curtailable at all times
flex.quote: FILLI Interconnection Service is subject to curtailment at all times

proximate.t: Does not adopt generation-linked mechanisms from other regions
proximate.quote: does not propose to replicate generation-linked mechanisms developed or proposed in other ISO/RTO regions

proximate.t: Proximity alone does not reduce transmission or resource adequacy needs
proximate.quote: physical proximity between load and generation does not guarantee reduced transmission requirements or resource adequacy obligations

study.quote: The definition includes a 50 MW load size which is reasonable for the New England transmission system.

study.t: $50,000 non-refundable application fee and $150,000 study deposit
study.quote: Initial, non-refundable application fee of $50,000 o Study deposit of $150,000

study.t: Final system impact study report within 120 days of the preliminary one
study.quote: publish a final Large Load System Impact Study report within 120 days of publishing the preliminary Large Load System Impact Study report

cost.t: Large Load Entity pays a Cost Recovery Charge so other customers' rates do not rise
cost.quote: so that there is no increase in transmission rates for other transmission customers caused by the interconnection of the Large Load Facility to the transmission system, the Large Load Entity will pay a Cost Recovery Charge

cost.t: Each load's network upgrades and their costs listed on ISO-NE's website
cost.quote: post on its website, in an easily accessible, searchable and fillable format: (1) a cumulative list reflecting the Large Load Network Upgrades identified for each Large Load

cost.t: A cost recovery agreement alone is insufficient to prevent cost shifting
cost.quote: the PTOs believe that a cost recovery agreement among ISO-NE, the relevant transmission owner, and the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of large loads is an insufficient guarantor

colo.t: No netting of behind-the-meter generation for wholesale settlement
colo.quote: Effectively, the Tariff Revisions prohibit the netting of a Large Load with Behind-the-Meter Generation for settlement of wholesale services.

colo.t: Netting threshold of zero MW, for large loads only
colo.quote: the ISO proposes a netting threshold of zero MW (which applies only to Large Loads).

flex.t: Interim Contract Demand Service for up to 7 years, or longer if the upgrades take longer
flex.quote: Interim Contract Demand Service shall be available for a term of no more than seven years, or the length of time required to place the required Large Load Network Upgrades in-service, whichever is longer

flex.t: Interim and non-firm service re-dispatched when price exceeds $250/MWh
flex.quote: all or a portion of a Large Load’s Interim Contract Demand Service and Non-Firm Contract Demand Service will be re-dispatched when the Large Load’s applicable LMP exceeds a Large Load Re-Dispatch Price of $250/MWh.

proximate.t: Proximate means the same substation and voltage level as the generator, narrower than the order's two substations
proximate.quote: Electrically Proximate Large Load is a configuration where a Large Load’s Point of Delivery is located at (or directly connected radially through dedicated facilities to) the same substation and voltage level as a Generating Facility’s Point of Interconnection

proximate.t: Expedited co-located and proximate generators kept out of the capacity market
proximate.quote: will not be counted towards the region’s capacity for resource adequacy purposes, will not participate in the capacity market

study.t: Large Load threshold: peak of 50 MW or more
study.quote: that has a peak Load of 50 MW or greater connected to the New York State Transmission System

study.t: Study cycle of 18 to 24 months, including a 90-day system impact study
study.quote: between one year and six months and two years, including a 90-day period for the performance of the System Impact Study

study.t: Existing load growing 10 MW+ after a change in use (e.g. to a data center) is restudied
study.quote: a smaller increase in the peak, gross load amount by 10 MW or greater compared to the baseline MW value

study.t: Study Deposits, site control and Readiness Deposits to deter speculative requests
study.quote: The inclusion of Study Deposits, Site Control requirements, and Readiness Deposits will assist in deterring speculative or duplicative submissions

cost.t: TOs recover 100% of allocated network upgrade and attachment facility costs
cost.quote: recover 100% of the costs of Network Upgrades and Attachment Facilities allocated to a Large Load Customer

cost.t: Customer posts security the TO can draw on abandonment or default
cost.quote: requires the Large Load Customer to post security for those allocated costs, which the Transmission Owner may draw upon in the event of abandonment of a Large Load project, default, or other specified events

cost.t: 20-year minimum revenue contribution per upgrade from its in-service date
cost.quote: MTRC Term begins on the actual Upgrade In-Service Date and ends on the day immediately preceding its twentieth anniversary

colo.t: Co-Located or Partner Resource Arrangement lets the load take firm withdrawal service
colo.quote: enter into a “Co-Located Arrangement” or “Partner Resource Arrangement” so that the Large Load may be served via some amount of Firm Withdrawal Service

colo.t: Does not adopt the three services from the PJM co-location order
colo.quote: Part V explains why the NYISO is not proposing to adopt the three new transmission services that the Commission established in the PJM Co-Location Order

flex.t: Firm and Non-Firm Withdrawal Service in place of the PJM services
Non-firm service curtailed when the local price reaches $200/MWh
flex.quote: Non-Firm Withdrawal Service would be curtailed when the applicable nodal Locational- Based Marginal Price (“LBMP”) for a Large Load reaches $200 MW/h

flex.t: Non-firm offered only where thermal or resource adequacy limits rule out firm service
flex.quote: Non-Firm Transmission Withdrawal Service may be offered only where thermal transmission constraints on Business Management System-secured facilities under N-1 and N-1-1 conditions, and/or resource adequacy violations, prevent the offering of Firm Transmission Withdrawal Service

proximate.t: Same Capacity Region test in place of the order's electrically proximate test
proximate.quote: use Associated Resource rules tied to NYISO Capacity Regions in lieu of the Show Cause Order’s “electrically proximate resource

proximate.t: A partner resource must sit in the same Capacity Region as the load
proximate.quote: for a Partner Resource Arrangement, the Resource must be located in the same Capacity Region as the given Large Load.
